title: A user write landing during a debounced in-flight solve is dropped: plan ignores it until the next interval
claim: When away, economy mode, a manual plan, a comfort-weight reset or a holiday-calendar change is written while a solve started through async_request_refresh (setup's first solve, a button, a service, any state listener) is in flight, the write's re-plan request is dropped by the refresh debouncer and the published plan stays built on the pre-write value until the next scheduled update: 7 of 8 request-refresh census rows stale, 0 of 8 when the in-flight solve came from async_refresh.
mechanism: DataUpdateCoordinator.async_request_refresh goes through Debouncer.async_call, which returns without arming a trailing run while a call is executing (upstream: 'Locked means a call is in progress. Any call is good, so abort.'; the stub mirrors it). The in-flight call is the refresh carrying the solve, so the writer's request never reaches async_run_optimization, whose #1754 re-run latch (_optimization_rerun_requested) only catches calls that arrive there. The scheduled interval refresh bypasses the debouncer, so the same write during a scheduled solve IS re-planned (null control). The stale window is up to one optimization_interval (default 30 min, DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL); _mode_superseded covers only the fixed modes.

evidence.unit: request-refresh census rows (of 8) whose write is not re-planned
evidence.machine: box B4 container, linux x86_64, Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: two arms of this harness and other finder seats running; a count, contention-immune

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._solve_record (entries counted after the write; the builder's output compared before/after), driven through HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_request_refresh / async_run_optimization on a real loop

perturbation.change: async_request_refresh records the #1754 re-run (self._optimization_rerun_requested = True) when self._optimization_running before deferring to the debouncer (harness flag --perturb-rerun)

metric_definition: Per d1-solve-state line whose writer re-plans via async_request_refresh: builder output changed by the write AND no _solve_record built after it before the loop settles.
phenomenon_property: Every re-plan request issued while a solve is in flight is honoured by one solve after that solve completes, whatever path (debounced or scheduled) started the in-flight solve.
seam_rule: grep -n 'async_request_refresh()' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (each caller that can run while a debounced refresh executes)

null_control.note: in-flight solve started by async_refresh (the scheduled interval's path): 0 of 8 stale; the 3 stale_plan_rows left in every arm are _peak_guard/_peak_tracker (power event) and _pv_export_price (no listener), which no writer re-plans by design and are picked up next cycle

reproduction_steps: set up on rl.RealHass, wait for the first solve
hold a solve in flight (gate on _run_in_process) started via async_request_refresh
run the row's writer (async_set_away, async_set_mode economy, async_apply_manual_plan, reset comfort + request refresh, holiday calendar state event)
release, settle: no _solve_record after the write; the plan is the pre-write one
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: override async_request_refresh (or the shared request path) to set _optimization_rerun_requested when a solve is in flight, so the in-flight solve's finally re-runs once (the perturbation).
